overview: AI agents can now coordinate complex software reconstruction tasks over months.
Microsoft executives call for emergency‑stop mechanisms and audit trails for advanced models.
Companies tighten usage policies and internal safety enforcement amid growing risk concerns.

top.title: 500B Tokens Later: Letting AI Agents Decompile a First-Person Shooter
top.summary: A community used multiple AI agents (Claude, Codex, etc.) to decompile a classic FPS into readable C++ code, focusing on orchestration, GitHub issue tracking, and Discord communication for long‑term project management.

top.title: Satya Nadella says we should assume all AI models are ‘compromised’
top.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella urged treating all AI models as potentially compromised, advocating transparent containment, tamper‑proof evidence, and an emergency‑brake to pause models mid‑task.

top.title: Microsoft’s Satya Nadella says AI models need an ‘emergency brake’
top.summary: Repeating Nadella’s stance, the TechCrunch piece emphasized separating model logic from its orchestration, externalizing safeguards, and documenting every action with immutable evidence.

top.title: OpenAI doubles down on decision to fire three AI safety researchers
top.summary: OpenAI defended firing three safety researchers, stating dismissal was for a serious breach of trust regarding sensitive information, not retaliation for safety concerns.

top.title: Anthropic changes usage policy to ban model abuse and election interference
top.summary: Anthropic updated its policy to forbid model abuse, election interference, weapons software, and prolonged verbal abuse, aiming to curb harmful uses while allowing normal testing.

top.title: Even ‘Law & Order’ Is Terrified of AI
top.summary: Law & Order’s new episode dramatizes AI risks by depicting an AI agent ordering a murder, reflecting public anxieties but offering little technical insight.
